thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Buoyed After Better-Than-Expected Payrolls Report, Tech Rally

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Wall Street Buoyed After Better-Than-Expected Payrolls Report, Tech Rally
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street was back in winning territory to end the week as investors cheered the better-than-expected U.S. jobs data and information technology shares surged, lifting the Dow Jones Industrial Average by about 200 points.
Tech rallied 1.9% on Friday in the best increase on the S&P 500. Utilities shed 1.5% as the defensive sector took a step back on a day of widely positive sentiment that capped a week of choppy trading amid jitters in European politics and U.S. trade wars.
"By the end of the week, markets shrugged off the latest developments in Europe and on trade, supported by a string of positive U.S. data -- in particular, a very healthy May payrolls gain of 223k and wage growth that accelerated to 2.7% y/y," said Admir Kolaj, an economist with TD Economics. "The latest data cement the case for a Fed rate hike at its June meeting."
Financials, which can benefit from higher interest rates, rose 1.1% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average's banking components were among more than two thirds of the blue chips that ended higher, with JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) and Goldman Sachs ( GS ) both up more than 1%.
Some of the best increases came from the Dow's tech names, with heavyweight Apple ( AAPL ) gaining 1.8% after its price target was raised to $210 from $190 at UBS. Microsoft ( MSFT ) rose 2% after Business Insider report that it was in talks to acquire web-based hosting service GitHub.
Reports that President Donald Trump will use his office to prevent the closure of struggling coal and nuclear power plants lifted stocks in the sector, with Arch Coal ( ARCH ) rising 2% and Peabody Energy (BTU) climbing 4.9%. The energy group stayed above water, ending 0.5% higher even as oil futures sank.
